# STRIP_LIST.md -- planconv's extra-strip list

> **HISTORICAL.** planconv no longer maintains a per-kind strip
> list. `NormalizeUnstructured` stripped only the fields below, which were
> derived from the 6 kinds in `testdata/charts/basic`, so any other workload
> kind (StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, ...) kept its server-side-defaulting
> fields and produced a permanent phantom diff. The live side now goes through
> `NormalizeLiveAgainst`, which projects each live object onto its planned
> counterpart's shape — dropping *every* field the chart didn't render, for
> every kind, generically. This file is retained as the evidence/rationale for
> why that projection is necessary; the fields it lists are exactly the
> server-side defaulting the projection now removes. The `.cleaned-diff.json`
> fixtures beside it are still used by `TestNormalizeGoldenPhantomDiff`.


Generated by `go run -tags smoke ./scripts/smoke/normalize` (the normalization golden pair). For every resource kind in testdata/charts/basic, this compares a LIVE cluster GET against the plan-After object from the first-install plan artifact, BOTH cleaned via `spec.CleanUnstruct(obj, CleanUnstructOptions{CleanRuntimeData: true, CleanHelmShAnnos: true, CleanWerfIoAnnos: true, CleanManagedFields: true})` -- the cleaning step of the normalization pipeline. Every JSON-pointer path listed below STILL differs after that cleaning and therefore MUST be additionally stripped by `planconv.NormalizeUnstructured`, or the very first `terraform plan` immediately after `terraform apply`/create would show a phantom diff against nothing having actually changed.

Per-resource raw evidence (both raw and CleanUnstruct-cleaned JSON, plus the exact RFC6902 diff) lives alongside this file under `internal/planconv/testdata/normalize/<Kind>.{live,planafter}.{raw,cleaned}.json` and `<Kind>.cleaned-diff.json`.

## Residual fields (union across all 6 resource kinds)

|---|---|---|
| `/metadata/annotations/deployment.kubernetes.io~1revision` | [Deployment] | strip unconditionally before marshaling canonical JSON |
| `/metadata/namespace` | [ConfigMap Secret Deployment Service] | strip unconditionally before marshaling canonical JSON |
| `/spec/clusterIP` | [Service] | strip unconditionally before marshaling canonical JSON |
| `/spec/clusterIPs` | [Service] | strip unconditionally before marshaling canonical JSON |

| `/spec/replicas` | [Deployment] | strip unconditionally before marshaling canonical JSON |
| `/spec/revisionHistoryLimit` | [Deployment] | strip unconditionally before marshaling canonical JSON |
| `/spec/sessionAffinity` | [Service] | strip unconditionally before marshaling canonical JSON |
| `/spec/strategy` | [Deployment] | strip unconditionally before marshaling canonical JSON |

## Caveat: `/spec/replicas` is NOT a strip candidate

Unlike every other row above, `/spec/replicas` is flagged here for a
different reason and must NOT be added to planconv's strip list. This
capture run (`scripts/smoke/normalize`) was executed against
`scripts/smoke/lifecycle`'s namespace/release AFTER lifecycle's step (c)
(the out-of-band `kubectl patch deployment ... replicas=3` drift fixture)
had already run against the same live Deployment, while the plan-After
value being compared against is from lifecycle's step (a) first-install
plan (captured before the release even existed, chart default
`replicaCount: 1`). So `1 -> 3` here is lifecycle's intentional drift
showing up correctly, not server-side defaulting noise -- it is exactly the
kind of REAL semantic difference `planconv.NormalizeUnstructured` must
continue to surface. Its presence in this diff is actually a useful
secondary confirmation: `CleanUnstruct` + the strip list above do not
accidentally erase genuine drift, they only remove fields Kubernetes itself
adds/defaults on the server side that were never in the chart's rendered
manifest to begin with.

## Field-by-field rationale (all real Kubernetes server-defaulting, confirmed against `kubectl explain`/API semantics)

- `metadata.namespace` -- the chart's rendered manifests never set an
  explicit namespace (helm convention: namespace comes from the release
  context), but any live GET always has it populated. Key resolution
  already accounts for this (`Key`'s `releaseNS` fallback), so it
  should also be stripped from the compared VALUE to avoid a values-level
  phantom diff on every single namespaced resource, every time.
- `metadata.annotations["deployment.kubernetes.io/revision"]` -- written by
  the deployment controller, never present in a pre-apply manifest.
- `spec.progressDeadlineSeconds`, `spec.revisionHistoryLimit`,
  `spec.strategy`, `spec.template.spec.dnsPolicy`,
  `spec.template.spec.restartPolicy`, `spec.template.spec.schedulerName`,
  `spec.template.spec.securityContext{}`,
  `spec.template.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds`,
  `spec.template.spec.containers[].terminationMessagePath`,
  `spec.template.spec.containers[].terminationMessagePolicy`,
  `spec.template.spec.containers[].resources{}`,
  `spec.template.spec.containers[].ports[].protocol` -- all standard
  apps/v1 Deployment / core/v1 PodSpec API server defaulting on create;
  none of these appear in a chart's raw rendered YAML unless the chart
  author set them explicitly (this chart doesn't).
- `spec.clusterIP`, `spec.clusterIPs`, `spec.ipFamilies`,
  `spec.ipFamilyPolicy`, `spec.internalTrafficPolicy`,
  `spec.sessionAffinity` -- standard core/v1 Service API server defaulting
  (cluster IP allocation and dual-stack/family/affinity defaults) on
  create; never present in a pre-apply manifest.

## Resource kinds with NO residual diff after `CleanUnstruct` alone

`ClusterRole` and `ClusterRoleBinding` (`rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1`, both
cluster-scoped -- the key-scoping case) required NO additional stripping: RBAC objects have no spec-level
server-side defaulting, so `CleanUnstruct{CleanRuntimeData, CleanHelmShAnnos,
CleanWerfIoAnnos, CleanManagedFields}` alone was already sufficient for
both of them.
